content_voiceover: This slide is a rapid-fire immunophenotype reference across the T- and NK-cell lymphomas, and it's worth memorizing the distinguishing features. T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia, T-LGLL, expresses CD2, CD3, CD8, CD57, and T-cell receptor alpha beta. T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia, T-PLL, is TdT negative, CD1a negative, with variable surface and cytoplasmic CD3, but characteristically CD5 positive, CD7 strongly positive, and CD52 strongly positive; most cases are CD4 positive, CD8 negative. Adult T-cell leukemia lymphoma, ATLL, is CD4 positive, CD5 positive, CD25 positive, but notably CD7 negative, which helps separate it from other CD4 positive T-cell neoplasms. Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma arises from gamma delta T cells, so it's typically T-cell receptor delta positive and T-cell receptor beta negative, CD4 and CD5 negative, with variable CD8 and CD56. Finally, extranodal NK slash T-cell lymphoma comes in two flavors: the classic NK-lineage form is surface CD3 negative but cytoplasmic CD3 epsilon positive, CD56 positive, EBER positive, with germline T-cell receptor genes, while the rarer T-lineage variant is surface CD3 positive with clonally rearranged TCR genes. The single most important discriminator across this whole group is EBER positivity, which defines ENKTL.
keypoints: T-LGLL: CD2/CD3/CD8/CD57, TCR alpha beta positive
T-PLL: CD5+, CD7++, CD52++; mostly CD4+/CD8-
HSTCL: gamma delta lineage, TCR delta+/TCR beta-, CD4-/CD5-
ENKTL: EBER+ defines it; NK-lineage is surface CD3-/cytoplasmic CD3+, CD56+
keypoint_voiceover: Five entities, five signatures. T-LGLL is CD8 and CD57 positive. T-PLL is CD7 and CD52 strongly positive. ATLL is CD4, CD5, CD25 positive but CD7 negative. Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma is the gamma delta one, TCR delta positive, TCR beta negative. And extranodal NK slash T-cell lymphoma is defined by EBER positivity, with surface CD3 negative but cytoplasmic CD3 epsilon positive marking the NK-lineage form.
